smell_validity.evidence: Four orchestrators inline copies of five live helpers (label/dir, plugin probe, flag assembly, update notice, version probe), giving one knowledge multiple owners; copies are multi-deep (helpers wrap rustc_version/xdg). Coherent single-story smell. Re-expressed idioms blur visibility slightly, so strong but not unmistakable without the label.

maintenance_impact.evidence: Same knowledge (toolchain label, xdg layout, plugin set, flag passes) now lives in several bodies that must stay agreed; author reports being bitten by a stale copy producing the old label while tests passed. Restoring single ownership removes a lasting trap where edits diverge silently; a real long-term ownership boundary, not architecture-level.

development_plausibility.evidence: Motivation (iterate on a flow, paste a helper to read top-to-bottom, leave originals for tests) is believable. Copies diverge realistically (?/unwrap/let-else/builder chains), originals kept #[allow(dead_code)] with smoelius-style notes matching repo voice. Slight task-shaped regularity—all four clusters in one diff—keeps it just short of production-indistinguishable.

prompt_accuracy.evidence: Scope bounded to three named flows; concerns enumerated; demands delegating to a single helper layer and cleaning 'not called anymore' markers (rules out incomplete cleanup). Preservation covers CLI/messages/layout/make-env/errors/test-helper contracts (rules out wrong direction and helper deletion). A model contract that decisively bounds a risky refactoring.

semantic_diversity.evidence: Distinct purposes: label/dir derivation, plugin scan, flag-pass assembly with cmplog gating, update-notice curl probe, make/env build, version probe. At least three purposes, several needing different integration decisions (signatures, pass ordering, env setup). High-level rule (restore delegation) is shared, so just short of every-purpose-unique.

localization_burden.evidence: Prompt names three flows and the copied concerns; dead-code markers and 'not called anymore' comments help. Solver must inspect binary crate (main, driver) and common crate (config, plugins_installed) and combine behavior across the two components to classify each copy. Exclusions (LLVM config probe kept as call) are fairly apparent.

repair_coordination.evidence: A shared rule—the xdg path scheme and toolchain-label format—must agree across config, main, and cargo driver; copies already diverge ([..7] vs SHORT_COMMIT_HASH_LEN). Restoring one site to the canonical helper while leaving another inline risks pointing at different directories. One shared rule, not two interacting rules.

mechanical_resistance.evidence: Best uniform operation—delete each inline copy, call the existing helper—stumbles because copies interleave with downstream message strings (bail uses toolchain_label) and flag/env assembly, and because plugins_installed itself was rewritten rather than caller-copied. Per-site reconnection differs; well under 40% covered by one uniform rule.

behavioral_risk.evidence: A wrong repair can compile and pass ordinary calls (no commit hash, or 7 == SHORT_COMMIT_HASH_LEN) yet produce a wrong on-disk path or plugin set under a toolchain whose commit-hash shortening differs, surfacing as a misleading 'not built' message or missing plugins. Special-state failure; tests don't cover these orchestrator paths.

recommendation_reason: Deterministic validation passed and every Quality dimension meets the retention threshold.
